text:
lina: quick check — after yesterday's demo i think we need to decide where the mux/shim does authz checks. keeping them in the frontend is easiest but feels risky for cache poisoning and N+1 calls
ash: agreed. frontend shortcuts are tempting but we lose a single source of truth. platform preference is server-side gate + lightweight client hints
tom: server gate + hints SGTM. can we keep a tiny optimistic cache in the UI for latency-sensitive panels? e.g., 500ms TTL, invalidated on route change
lina: yeah optimistic cache could work, but we have to be explicit about stale UI states. UX will need a spinner fallback. no silent wrong data
kevin: from infra: server-side gate lets us centralize rate limiting/backpressure. if we do server-side, we can also apply bulk authz checks batching across panels
ash: batching is key. current panel renderer does 6 parallel queries per page. if each query asks authz separately that's 6x overhead. want an authz multiplexer in the query router
lin a: (typo) lina: ^^^ multiplexer in the router makes sense. tradeoff: added router complexity, slightly increased critical path for cold requests
ash: acceptable if we make multiplexer async and return provisional permission set. flow: 1) page requests panel manifests 2) client posts permission probe to /authz-mux 3) router returns permissions map + indicators for 'pending'
tom: example API sketch:
```
POST /authz-mux
body: { panels: [ {id, resource, action} ] }
response: { perms: { panelId: true/false/pending }, version: "v1" }
```
kevin: infra note: need to propagate request origin to the backend services for any downstream audit logs. also tie perms to token version so cache invalidation is safe
lina: about backpressure: if authz checks lag (DB throttled) do we let panels render with placeholders or block whole page? product wants partial render
ash: partial render. block only if more than 40% of critical panels missing or if primary panel permission unknown. we should have a graceful degrade policy baked in config
tom: config snippet idea:
```
ui.authz.degrade_threshold=0.4
ui.authz.optimistic_cache_ms=500
router.authz.batch_window_ms=50
```
kevin: also add a circuit-breaker metric histogram so ops can see authz latency tail. default policy should fallback to deny for high-severity resources
ash: rollout plan: feature-flag mux behind canary. start with 10% tenant routing, compare latencies and authz error rates for 2 weeks. ops alert if 99th latency regresses > 25%
lin a: lina: who owns the UX copy for the placeholder? also need accessibility text when panels are gated
kevin: assign to me and @tom for accessibility review. i'll schedule a quick design handoff
tom: i'll add instrumentation for per-panel authz timing and a synthetic that exercises mux batch paths
ash: action items:
- ash: write router multiplexer prototype and POC (ETA 1w)
- tom: add authz timing metrics + synth (ETA 3d)
- kevin: add circuit-breaker and audit propagation plan (ETA 1w)
- lina: coordinate UX copy + spinner behavior (ETA 4d)
infra-bot: deploy-canary: scheduled canary rollout for 10% traffic on 2026-05-05T08:00Z (job 4992) :rocket:
kevin: one last thing — update the security doc with explicit mention that client-side optimistic caches are considered UI-only and not authoritative
lina: ok thanks everyone, i'll capture notes and link a small RFC in #eng-platform for the mux contract and gating rules
ash: nice. we should also add a unit test in panel renderer that simulates pending perms path
kevin: ack
